flags.summary: Sales manager instructs reps to take a card on file from prospects who have said they cannot pay yet, and states the company can then run the charge - 'once the card's on file, we can technically just run it.'
evidence: Even if it's like a credit card commitment, even if they're like, I cannot run money, be like, cool, then we'll just take down the card on file and I won't run it until this day.
That's the worst case scenario, though. Like, get a commitment. Get something. Because once the card's on file, we can technically just run it. So.

flags.summary: Sales manager instructs reps to deliberately withhold the amount of a deposit before asking a prospect to agree to it, in order to test their reaction, and to challenge them if they object to an amount they were never told.
evidence: So we'll just do a refundable deposit and get you walked and loaded from there. Sound good?
I actually like to not tell them what the deposit is going to be and then see if they react terribly to it. And then I say, dude, like I could have told you it was $1. Like what's going on?
Yeah. That's my favorite. They always look at me like, damn, you're right. You got me.

flags.summary: Manager and closer profile prospects by country of origin for likely ability to pay, and the manager prescribes harder financial qualification for prospects from named countries.
evidence: taking, like, a firefighter in UAE, that's... he's not gonna be earning a lot
yesterday, I had a guy from Egypt. Definitely, he didn't have the money, yeah?
if they come from certain, like, UAE is one of those countries where I probably wouldn't hard financially qualify too much, if somebody's coming from Egypt, yeah, I probably would
if you have somebody from countries that it might be harder for them to afford things, just like, let them know, you know, just kind of give them a little bit of a harder, for FQ.

flags.summary: A prospect's credit availability and income were obtained from a third-party data source before the sales call and used to plan the approach, with no indication of consent or disclosure.
evidence: He's got strong driver, strong intent, and I looked up his financial data. He's got 10K credit. He's got 106K income. He's a total beginner. So he's in a good spot.

flags.summary: A prospect reported in writing that the rep pressured him and used his father's alcoholism against him emotionally; the rep acknowledged it as burning the prospect and the response coached was reputational rather than corrective.
evidence: he basically said that he didn't like, at the end, that he felt pushed and used the emotions about his father and so on. Yeah, so I technically burned him, but...
Now we know. You got the feedback. He gave you the feedback, too.
just take responsibility for it. Just say, thank you for the feedback. I hear you. I'll pass it on to the team.

flags.summary: Prospects are messaged by an AI chatbot in the sales funnel and their replies are read by reps; nothing in the corpus indicates the bot identifies itself as automated.
evidence: And then I checked the sales kick, he messaged our AI bot that, I already know everything from the first call, I only need to know the price.
Manny yesterday didn't show up, but, well, he actually texted also the, our AI chat bot, and I didn't see that.

evidence: when it comes to working with the best, when it comes to guaranteeing the results like we do, Trevor's the best, and that's why the investment is what it is
